# {{projectName}} — ModMon Modular Monolith

This repository was scaffolded by the ModMon CLI. It is a .NET modular
monolith: one deployable API composed of isolated vertical-slice modules
plus a shared kernel.

## Layout

```
{{projectName}}.sln
{{projectName}}.Api/            # entry point: Program.cs, DI aggregator, Serilog
{{projectName}}.SharedKernel/   # shared contracts, base entities, middleware, events
{{projectName}}.<Module>/       # one folder per business module (own DbContext)
Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml  # SDK 10.0 build -> aspnet noble-chiseled runtime
.dockerignore, .gitignore       # image build + repo hygiene
AGENTS.md                       # top-level agent guidance
.agents/skills/modmon/          # this skill
```

## Boundary rules (enforced by `modmon validate`)

| Project | May reference |
| --- | --- |
| `{{projectName}}.Api` | Modules + `{{projectName}}.SharedKernel` |
| `{{projectName}}.<Module>` | `{{projectName}}.SharedKernel` only |
| `{{projectName}}.SharedKernel` | No API or module projects |

`validate` checks the project-reference graph and required files — not C#
source usage. Modules must never reference each other or the API.

## Commands that matter here

```bash
modmon module add --name <Module>   # scaffold a module + wire it in
modmon module list                  # detected modules
modmon info                         # project + modules overview
modmon validate                     # structure + boundary checks
modmon <cmd> --format json          # machine-readable output
modmon <cmd> --path <dir>           # run against another repo root
modmon module add --dry-run         # preview without writing
```

Exit codes: `0` ok, `2` bad args, `3` already exists, `4` not found,
`5` validation failed, `6` dotnet/dotnet-ef error, `7` filesystem,
`8` network.

## `module add` — what it changes

- Creates `{{projectName}}.<Module>/` (DbContext, design-time factory, DI
  extension, DbUp scripts + `DbUpMigrator`, standard folders), adds it to
  the solution, and references it from the API project.
- Inserts registrations into
  `{{projectName}}.Api/Extensions/DependencyInjection.cs` between markers
  and adds a `COPY` line to the Dockerfile between `# <modules>` markers.
- Runs `dotnet ef migrations add InitialCreate` into
  `Database/Migrations/` — requires the `dotnet-ef` tool; if it is
  missing the module is still added, with a `warnings` entry.
- On failure it rolls back: restores the DI aggregator and Dockerfile,
  removes solution/reference entries, deletes the module folder.

**Never remove the markers** — `// <modules>`, `// <ef>`, `// <dbup>` in
the DI aggregator and `# <modules>` in the Dockerfile. Without them
`module add` cannot wire new modules and emits a warning instead.

## Database migrations — two systems, fixed order

`Program.cs` calls `app.ApplyProjectMigrations(configuration)`:

1. `// <ef>` — EF Core migrations (`Database.Migrate()`) own entity
   schema: tables, columns, indexes from each module's DbContext.
2. `// <dbup>` — DbUp scripts own supplemental objects: views,
   functions, seed data (`Database/Scripts/Versioned` + `Repeatable`).

**Ownership rule:** never let both systems manage the same object. If EF
migrations create a table, no DbUp script may recreate it — the second
runner fails.

## Cross-module communication

Modules never touch each other's DbContext or internals. Share contracts
through `{{projectName}}.SharedKernel`: an `I{Thing}Service` interface
implemented by the owning module, or an `IEvent` dispatched via the
registered `IEventDispatcher`. Full patterns and code:
`architecture-patterns.md`.
